To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the change in the tree growth–temperature relationship is similar between latitudinal gradient and altitudinal gradient, but there are differences in the timing of climate variables that have the strongest effects on tree growth.

the change of the growth–climate relation is similar along both the latitudinal as well as the altitudinal gradients and that the time period during which climate affects the growth most occurs later towards higher latitudinal and higher altitudinal positions.

the growth–climate signal of tree rings is similar along latitudinal gradients and altitudinal gradient, but the time periods during the growing season when the climate has its most significant impact on tree growth vary along both gradients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question whether latitudinal and alitudinal gradients are similar in their impact on tree growth and its climate response.
the impact of climate and environmental factors on tree growth along latitudinal gradients in Finland and on altitudinal gradients in the Tibetan Plateau and the differences between them.
the impact of climate and climate change on tree growth along environmental gradients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the latitudinal gradients are similar in their climate–tree growth relationship to altitudinal gradients in terms of the effect of temperature.

both latitudinal gradients and altitude gradients have similar climate–growth responses, but also that the climate–growth relationships differ in the timing of critical climate variables between gradients.
the growth–climate signal is stronger at higher latitudes and higher altitudes, but the exact pattern depends on the specific climate variables and the moisture conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
latitudinal and altitude gradients are useful tools for studying the effects of environmental factors on tree growth.
the latitudinal gradients are more suitable to study the effects of climate on tree growth than the altitudinal gradients.
the latitudinal gradients can serve as a model for understanding the altitudinal gradients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the latitudinal gradients can serve as a proxy for altitudinal gradients for the prediction of forest growth responses to climate change.
latitudinal gradients may not necessarily be the best proxies for altitudinal gradients in the context of tree growth–climate relationships.
